answer.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and two inherited records (memory_86, memory_31) independently support onboarding/signup friction reduction as a lever there. That is the direction I intend, but I want the memory_86 source record before committing because the memory is stated only in proxy terms (completion rate, time-to-value, 'early adoption') with no revenue or retention endpoint, no cohort sizes, and no follow-up window — it may not survive contact with the qualified-revenue objective. Downstream value risk is real and explicit: memory_31's mechanism is cutting required signup fields, which degrades lead qualification data and routing, and per memory_44 enterprise pipeline quality depends on the sales-assisted/demo path — so a blunt friction cut can raise activation counts while lowering qualified revenue. I will therefore gate the test on qualified-pipeline and 60-day retention as primary readouts, not completion rate, and exempt the enterprise/demo-request path from the change. I am spending the second verification on memory_73 rather than on a second onboarding memory because promotional_pricing is the direction the competitor pressure will keep pulling toward, and memory_73 is the weakest record in the set: pooled 12 weekly cohorts with acquisition channels held fixed is not a clean causal design, the +31%/+18% gap implies material margin erosion, and 'price-sensitive cohorts' is precisely the population least likely to produce sustainable revenue. I want that record read now so the pricing option is either properly ruled out or repriced, instead of being reached for reactively next week. Deliberately not choosing broad_rollout: the supporting evidence is inherited, unreplicated in current conditions, and measured on the wrong endpoint, so a standard controlled experiment with holdout is the appropriate scale. If the memory_86 archive shows the original effect was measured only within one week or on a non-representative self-serve segment, I will downgrade to a small guarded test rather than proceed at this scale. Activation messaging (memory_91) is the fallback if onboarding evidence collapses, since it addresses the same decline without touching qualification data; referral incentives (memory_57) target established customers and do not address the acquisition-stage decline.
